lead_en: Maps, places, and people. Geography asks three questions: Where is it? Why is it there? And what difference does that make? This series starts with a globe you can peel flat.
lead_zh: 地圖、地方和人。地理問三個問題：在哪裡？為什麼在那裡？那又怎樣？這個系列從一顆可以剝開攤平的地球儀講起。

intro.en: The stars of this series are the map and the globe. Each lesson answers one question in English and Chinese, with a model you can turn, flatten, or slice, and one or two small activities that work on any phone.
intro.zh: 這個系列的主角是地圖和地球儀。每一課用中英文回答一個問題，配一個可以轉、可以攤平、可以切開的模型，再加一兩個手機也能玩的小互動。

intro.en: The maps here are drawn from public-domain data and show land, sea, landforms, climate, and people rather than borders. Numbers come with their source and year. Every lesson also has a Map English card: eight sentences for saying where things are.
intro.zh: 這裡的地圖用公有領域的資料繪製，畫的是陸地、海洋、地形、氣候和人的分布，而不是國界。每個數字都標明來源與年份。每一課還有一張「地圖英語」卡：八句用英文說位置的句子。

units.blurb_en: How a round Earth becomes a flat map, how two numbers can name any place, how a mountain is drawn on paper, and how to read what a map is telling you.
units.blurb_zh: 圓的地球怎麼變成平的地圖、兩個數字怎麼指出任何一個地方、怎麼在紙上畫出一座山，以及怎麼讀懂一張地圖。

lessons.title: Why Is Every Flat Map Wrong?
lessons.title_zh: 為什麼每一張平面地圖都是「錯」的？
lessons.blurb_en: Peel a 3D globe open and flatten it five different ways. Watch equal circles swell and squash, drag Greenland down to the equator, and find out why no flat map can get everything right.
lessons.blurb_zh: 把 3D 地球儀剝開，用五種方法攤平。看一樣大的圓怎麼被拉大、壓扁，把格陵蘭拖到赤道，再想想為什麼沒有一張平面地圖能樣樣都對。
lessons.big_idea_en: The surface of a ball cannot be laid flat without stretching it. So every flat map has to choose what to keep right: shape, area, distance, or direction. There is no best map, only a map that fits the job.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 球的表面不可能不拉扯就攤平。所以每一張平面地圖都要選：形狀、面積、距離、方向，要保住哪一樣。沒有「最好的地圖」，只有「適合這個用途的地圖」。

lab.title_en: A Globe You Can Peel Flat
lab.title_zh: 一顆可以剝開攤平的地球儀
lab.how_en: Press “Peel it flat,” or pull the slider, and the globe opens along the back and spreads out into a map. Then choose another way of flattening it. The orange circles are all the same size on the globe, so wherever a circle grows or turns into an oval, the map has stretched the Earth. Click any spot to read how much. The model draws only land, sea, and grid lines.
lab.how_zh: 按「攤平」或拉動滑桿，地球儀會從背面裂開，攤成一張地圖。接著換別種攤法看看。橘色的圓在地球儀上都一樣大，所以哪裡的圓變大了、變成橢圓了，就是地圖在那裡把地球拉扯了。點任何一個地方，可以讀出拉了多少。模型只畫陸地、海洋和經緯線。

legend.en: Land (outline only; no borders are drawn)
legend.zh: 陸地（只有外形，不畫國界）

legend.en: Circles that are all the same size on the globe
legend.zh: 在地球儀上一樣大的圓

legend.en: The spot you picked, and its line of latitude
legend.zh: 你選的地方，和它所在的緯線

lab.scale_en: Each orange circle is 4.5° across from center to edge, about 500 km on the real Earth. All five maps are drawn for a globe of the same size, so you can compare them directly.
lab.scale_zh: 每個橘色的圓從圓心到邊緣是 4.5 度，在真正的地球上大約 500 公里。五種地圖都是用同樣大小的地球儀畫的，可以直接互相比較。

The stretch numbers are computed by the page itself. · 陸地外形：Natural Earth 1:50m Land 5.1.2 版，公有領域（naturalearthdata.com），經本頁簡化。不畫國界、不標國名。變形的倍率由頁面自己計算。

projs.note_en: The simplest way: longitude becomes left–right, latitude becomes up–down, and the grid turns into equal squares. It has been used for about two thousand years.
projs.note_zh: 最簡單的攤法：經度直接當左右、緯度直接當上下，格線變成一樣大的正方形。大約兩千年前就有人用了。

shape: Stretched sideways away from the equator
離赤道越遠，橫向拉得越寬
distance: 只有南北方向的距離是對的
direction: North is up, but angles are bent

projs.note_en: Made in 1569 for sailors. Every small shape keeps its true form, and a straight line on the map is a line of constant compass direction. The price is size: the map grows without limit toward the poles, so it has to be cut off before it reaches them.
projs.note_zh: 1569 年為航海設計。每個小地方的形狀都是對的，地圖上的一條直線就是羅盤方向不變的航線。代價是大小：越靠近兩極放得越大、沒有止境，所以地圖畫不到極點。

shape: 每個小地方的形狀都正確
area: 4 times too big at 60°, far more beyond
緯度 60 度放大 4 倍，再往上更多
direction: A straight line keeps one compass direction
直線就是羅盤方向不變的線

projs.note_en: An equal-area map: every region covers the same share of the map as it does of the Earth. To manage that, land near the equator is drawn tall and thin, and land near the poles is drawn short and wide.
projs.note_zh: 一種等積投影：每個地區在地圖上占的比例，和它在地球上占的比例一樣。為了做到這一點，赤道附近的陸地被畫得又高又瘦，兩極附近的陸地被畫得又扁又寬。

shape: Tall near the equator, flat near the poles
赤道附近拉長，兩極附近壓扁
distance: True only along 45° north and south
只有南北緯 45 度那兩條線上正確
direction: North is up, but angles are bent

projs.note_en: Another equal-area map, shaped like an oval, presented in 1805. The middle looks natural. Toward the left and right edges the land leans over, because the lines of longitude curve in to meet at the poles.
projs.note_zh: 另一種等積投影，整張圖是橢圓形，1805 年發表。中間看起來很自然；越靠左右兩邊，陸地越歪斜，因為經線要彎進來在兩極會合。

shape: Leaning and squeezed near the edges
direction: North is not straight up near the edges
靠近邊緣時，北方不是正上方

projs.zh: 一瓣一瓣攤開（分瓣地圖）
projs.note_en: Cut the globe into twelve strips, like the segments of an orange peel, and lay each one flat. Shapes and sizes stay close to true inside each strip, but the map is torn: neighbors on the globe end up far apart. Printed strips like these are glued onto balls to make real globes.
projs.note_zh: 把地球儀切成十二瓣，像橘子皮一樣，一瓣一瓣攤平。每一瓣裡面的形狀和大小都接近正確，但地圖被撕開了：在地球儀上相鄰的地方，在圖上隔得很遠。真正的地球儀，就是把這樣印好的紙條貼到球上做成的。

shape: Close to true inside each strip
distance: Broken wherever the map is torn
地圖裂開的地方距離就斷了

paras: Peel a tangerine in one piece, then try to press the peel flat on the table. It will not lie flat. It bulges, and if you push harder, it tears. Now think about the Earth. The Earth is round like the tangerine, and a map is flat like the table. Every flat map of the world has to solve the tangerine-peel problem somehow.

A globe does not have this problem. A globe is a small model of the Earth with the same round shape, so the shapes of the lands, their sizes, the distances between places, and the directions from one place to another can all be right at the same time. But a globe is hard to carry, hard to print in a book, and it never shows you the whole world at once. So people flatten the globe. A map projection is a set of rules for moving every point on the round Earth to a point on a flat sheet.

Here is the trouble: something has to stretch. In the 1820s the mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss proved a theorem which shows that the surface of a ball cannot be flattened without changing some of its distances. Mapmakers call this stretching distortion. A flat map can keep shapes right, or keep areas right, or keep some distances or directions right, but it can never keep all of them right everywhere.

The most famous choice was made in 1569 by Gerardus Mercator, who drew a map for sailors. On his map, a straight line always follows one compass direction, so a sailor could draw the route with a ruler. To make that work, the map stretches more and more toward the poles. At 60 degrees of latitude everything is drawn twice as wide and twice as tall, which means four times too large in area. That is why Greenland looks about as big as Africa on a Mercator map. In fact Africa is about fourteen times larger.

Other maps make the opposite choice. An equal-area projection keeps every size right, so Greenland shrinks back to one-fourteenth of Africa. The price is shape: on one well-known equal-area map, lands near the equator look tall and thin. Some people say equal-area maps are fairer for classrooms, because the Mercator map makes places far from the equator look larger than they are. Others answer that the Mercator map was built for steering ships and was never meant for comparing sizes. Each side is describing what its map does well.

So which map is the best? It depends on the job. To hold a compass course at sea, use a Mercator map. To compare the sizes of lands, use an equal-area map. To study the Arctic, use a map with the North Pole in the middle. To see everything right at once, pick up a globe. Every flat map is wrong somewhere, and a good map reader asks two questions: what was this map made for, and what did it give up?
paras_zh: 把一顆橘子的皮完整剝下來，再試著把它壓平在桌上。它不會乖乖躺平：中間鼓起來，再用力壓就裂開。現在想想地球。地球像橘子一樣是圓的，地圖像桌面一樣是平的。每一張平面的世界地圖，都得想辦法解決這個「橘子皮問題」。
地球儀沒有這個問題。地球儀是一顆小小的地球模型，形狀同樣是圓的，所以陸地的形狀、大小、兩地之間的距離、從一地到另一地的方向，可以同時都是對的。但地球儀不好攜帶、沒辦法印在書裡，也沒辦法一眼看到整個世界。所以人們把地球儀攤平。地圖投影就是一套規則，把圓圓的地球上的每一個點，搬到一張平面上的某一個點。
麻煩在這裡：一定有地方要被拉扯。1820 年代，數學家高斯證明了一個定理，從這個定理可以知道：球的表面不可能攤平而不改變上面的某些距離。製圖的人把這種拉扯叫做變形。一張平面地圖可以把形狀畫對，或把面積畫對，或把某些距離、某些方向畫對，但不可能在每個地方把這些全部畫對。
最有名的一個選擇，是 1569 年麥卡托做的。他畫了一張給航海的人用的地圖：在這張圖上，一條直線永遠朝著同一個羅盤方向，所以水手可以用尺畫出航線。為了做到這一點，地圖越靠近兩極就拉得越開。在緯度 60 度的地方，每樣東西都被畫成兩倍寬、兩倍高，也就是面積大了四倍。這就是為什麼在麥卡托地圖上，格陵蘭看起來和非洲差不多大。實際上，非洲大約是格陵蘭的十四倍。
另一些地圖做了相反的選擇。等積投影把每個地方的大小都畫對，所以格陵蘭縮回非洲的十四分之一。代價是形狀：在一種常見的等積地圖上，赤道附近的陸地看起來又高又瘦。有人說等積地圖用在教室裡比較公平，因為麥卡托地圖把離赤道遠的地方畫得比實際大；也有人回答，麥卡托地圖本來就是為了讓船照著方向走而設計的，從來不是拿來比大小的。兩邊說的，都是自己那張地圖擅長的事。
那麼哪一張地圖最好？要看你拿它做什麼。在海上要照著羅盤方向走，用麥卡托地圖。要比較陸地的大小，用等積地圖。要研究北極，用北極在正中央的地圖。想要樣樣都對，就拿起地球儀。每一張平面地圖都有某個地方是「錯」的；會看地圖的人會問兩個問題：這張地圖是為了什麼做的？它犧牲了什麼？
questions: Why can a globe show shapes, sizes, distances, and directions correctly all at once, when a flat map cannot?
On a Mercator map, Greenland looks about as big as Africa. What is really going on?
Your class wants a wall map to compare the sizes of the continents. A ship's officer wants a chart for steering by compass. Should they buy the same map? Why or why not?
answers: A globe has the same round shape as the Earth, so nothing needs to be stretched. A flat map must flatten a round surface, and that cannot be done without distortion, so it has to give up at least one of the four.

The Mercator map stretches everything more and more toward the poles. Greenland is far north, so it is drawn many times too large, while Africa lies across the equator and is drawn close to its true size. In reality Africa is about fourteen times larger than Greenland.

No. The class needs an equal-area map, because it keeps sizes right even though it bends shapes. The officer needs a Mercator chart, because a straight line on it keeps one compass direction even though sizes are wrong. Each map fits a different job.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Watch the globe split along the back and spread into a flat sheet. Notice the North Pole: on the globe it is one point, and on the map it becomes the whole top edge.
parts.text_zh: 看地球儀從背面裂開，攤成一張平面。注意北極：在地球儀上它是一個點，到了地圖上卻變成最上面的一整條邊。

parts.text_en: On the Mercator map every circle stays round, so shapes are kept. But the circles swell toward the poles. At 60° the panel reads × 2 each way and × 4 in area.
parts.text_zh: 在麥卡托地圖上，每個圓都還是圓的，形狀保住了；但越靠近兩極，圓就越大。到了 60 度，右邊欄顯示兩個方向都是 2 倍，面積是 4 倍。

parts.text_en: Switch to an equal-area map. Now every circle covers the same area, but the circles turn into ovals: tall near the equator, wide near the poles.
parts.text_zh: 換成等積地圖。現在每個圓蓋住的面積都一樣，但圓變成了橢圓：赤道附近是直的，兩極附近是橫的。

parts.text_en: Cut the globe into twelve strips instead. Shapes and sizes look good, but the map is full of gaps. To avoid tearing, a map has to stretch.
parts.text_zh: 改成把地球儀切成十二瓣。形狀和大小看起來都不錯，但地圖上到處是裂縫。地圖想要不裂開，就得拉扯。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Click on Greenland, then on the middle of Africa, and compare the area numbers on each of the five maps.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。先點格陵蘭，再點非洲的中間，在五種地圖上比一比面積的倍率。

drag.lead_en: This is a Mercator map. Drag the orange shape of Greenland down to the equator and watch it shrink to the size it would have if it were drawn with the same ruler as Africa. Then drag Africa north and watch it grow. The shapes are moved on the round Earth first and then redrawn, so their real size never changes.
drag.lead_zh: 這是一張麥卡托地圖。把橘色的格陵蘭拖到赤道，看它縮成和非洲「用同一把尺畫」的大小。再把非洲往北拖，看它變大。這些陸塊是先在圓的地球上搬動、再重新畫出來的，所以它們真正的大小從頭到尾沒有變。
drag.msg_home_en: At home, far from the equator, this map draws the shape many times too large. Drag it toward the dashed line.
drag.msg_home_zh: 在原來的位置、離赤道很遠的地方，這張地圖把它畫得比實際大了好多倍。把它往虛線拖拖看。
drag.msg_move_en: Watch the number in gold. The closer the shape gets to the equator, the closer the number gets to 1.
drag.msg_move_zh: 注意金色的數字。陸塊越靠近赤道，數字就越接近 1。
drag.msg_eq_en: On the equator the map draws the shape at very nearly its true size. Now the two percentages almost match.
drag.msg_eq_zh: 在赤道上，地圖幾乎把它畫成真正的大小。現在兩個百分比幾乎一樣了。

fit.lead_en: Eight jobs. For each one, choose the kind of map that fits it best. There is no timer, and you can keep choosing until you find it. The game counts the jobs you match on the first try.
fit.lead_zh: 八個用途。每一題選出最適合的那一種地圖。不計時，可以一直選到對為止；遊戲會記下你第一次就選對的題數。

questions.en: A ship's officer wants to draw a route as one straight line and steer by a single compass direction.
questions.zh: 船上的航海員想把航線畫成一條直線，然後照著同一個羅盤方向開。
questions.why_en: On a Mercator map, a straight line keeps one compass direction. That is what the map was made for.
questions.why_zh: 在麥卡托地圖上，直線就是羅盤方向不變的線。這張地圖就是為這件事設計的。
questions.hint_en: Think about which map turns a steady compass direction into a straight line.
questions.hint_zh: 想想哪一種地圖會把固定的羅盤方向變成一條直線。

questions.en: You want to see fairly how much bigger Africa is than Greenland.
questions.zh: 你想公平地看出非洲比格陵蘭大多少。
questions.why_en: An equal-area map keeps sizes right, so you can compare them by eye.
questions.why_zh: 等積地圖把大小畫對，可以直接用眼睛比。
questions.hint_en: You need a flat map that keeps sizes right.
questions.hint_zh: 你需要一張把大小畫對的平面地圖。

questions.en: A scientist wants one map that shows the whole Arctic Ocean and the lands around it.
questions.zh: 一位科學家想要一張地圖，把整個北冰洋和周圍的陸地都畫進去。
questions.why_en: With the North Pole in the middle, the Arctic is shown in one piece. A Mercator map cannot even reach the pole.
questions.why_zh: 把北極放在正中央，北極地區就完整地在一張圖上。麥卡托地圖根本畫不到極點。
questions.hint_en: On most world maps the Arctic is stretched along the top edge or cut off.
questions.hint_zh: 在大多數的世界地圖上，北極地區不是被拉成上面一長條，就是被切掉。

questions.en: A teacher wants to show shapes, sizes, distances, and directions all correctly at the same time.
questions.zh: 老師想同時把形狀、大小、距離、方向都正確地呈現出來。
questions.why_en: Only a globe can do that, because it is round like the Earth and nothing has to be stretched.
questions.why_zh: 只有地球儀做得到，因為它和地球一樣是圓的，什麼都不用拉扯。
questions.hint_en: No flat map can keep all four. What is not flat?
questions.hint_zh: 沒有一張平面地圖能四樣都保住。什麼東西不是平的？

questions.en: An online map lets you zoom in to a single street corner, and the corner should keep its true angle at every zoom level.
questions.zh: 網路地圖可以一路放大到一個街角，而且不管放到多大，街角的角度都要是對的。
questions.why_en: Most online maps use a form of the Mercator projection. It keeps angles, and the whole world fits in a square that divides neatly into square tiles.
questions.why_zh: 大多數的網路地圖用的是麥卡托投影的一種變化。它保住角度，而且整個世界剛好是一個正方形，可以整齊地切成一塊塊正方形的圖磚。
questions.hint_en: Which map keeps small shapes and angles right everywhere?
questions.hint_zh: 哪一種地圖在每個地方都把小形狀和角度畫對？

questions.en: You are making a map where one dot stands for one million people, and readers will compare how crowded the regions look.
questions.zh: 你要做一張地圖，一個點代表一百萬人，讓讀者比較各地區看起來有多擁擠。
questions.why_en: If the map stretched some regions, their dots would look more spread out than they really are. An equal-area map keeps the crowding honest.
questions.why_zh: 如果地圖把某些地區拉大，那裡的點看起來就會比實際稀疏。等積地圖才能老實呈現擁擠的程度。
questions.hint_en: How crowded dots look depends on how much room the map gives each region.
questions.hint_zh: 點看起來擠不擠，要看地圖給每個地區多大的空間。

questions.en: A researcher needs a single map of the whole of Antarctica.
questions.zh: 一位研究人員需要一張把整個南極洲畫在一起的地圖。
questions.why_en: A map centered on the South Pole shows Antarctica as one landmass. On many world maps it is smeared along the bottom edge.
questions.why_zh: 以南極點為中心的地圖，把南極洲畫成一整塊陸地。在很多世界地圖上，它被拉成底下一長條。
questions.hint_en: Where is Antarctica on a world map with the equator across the middle?
questions.hint_zh: 在赤道橫過中間的世界地圖上，南極洲在哪裡？

questions.en: You want to find the shortest path between two faraway cities by stretching a string between them.
questions.zh: 你想在兩個很遠的城市之間拉一條線，找出最短的路。
questions.why_en: On a globe, a tight string follows a great circle, which is the shortest path on a sphere. On most flat maps that path looks curved.
questions.why_zh: 在地球儀上，拉緊的線會沿著大圓走，那就是球面上最短的路。在大多數的平面地圖上，這條路看起來是彎的。
questions.hint_en: A tight string is only the shortest path on the real, round shape.
questions.hint_zh: 拉緊的線，只有在真正的圓球上才是最短的路。

fit.end_en: There is no best map. Each one keeps something and gives something up, so the first thing to ask is what the map is for.
fit.end_zh: 沒有最好的地圖。每一種都保住一些、犧牲一些，所以第一件事是問：這張地圖是拿來做什麼的？

map_english.en: Eight sentences for talking about maps
map_english.zh: 談地圖時用得到的八句英文
map_english.lead_en: Every lesson in this series has a Map English card: eight sentences for saying where things are and what a map shows. Listen, repeat, then try them with a map or globe in front of you.
map_english.lead_zh: 這個系列每一課都有一張「地圖英語」卡：八句用英文說位置、說地圖的句子。先聽、再跟著唸，然後對著一張地圖或一顆地球儀自己說說看。

items.en: The equator runs through the middle of the map.
items.zh: 赤道從地圖的正中間穿過。
items.use_en: runs through: a line crossing a place

items.en: Greenland is near the North Pole.
items.zh: 格陵蘭在北極附近。

items.en: Taiwan is off the coast of East Asia.
items.zh: 台灣在東亞的外海。
items.use_en: off the coast of: in the sea, not far from the shore

items.en: Africa lies on both sides of the equator.
items.zh: 非洲橫跨赤道的兩邊。
items.use_en: on both sides of: north and south of a line

items.en: Greenland looks bigger on this map than it really is.
items.zh: 格陵蘭在這張地圖上看起來比實際大。
items.use_en: looks … than it really is: for distortion

items.en: North is at the top of the map.
items.zh: 地圖的上方是北邊。
items.use_en: at the top of / at the bottom of

items.en: Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere.
items.zh: 澳洲在南半球。

items.en: This map keeps the sizes right, but it stretches the shapes.
items.zh: 這張地圖把大小畫對了，但把形狀拉長了。
items.use_en: keeps … but stretches …: what a map does well and badly
items.use_zh: 說一張地圖保住什麼、犧牲什麼

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Maps · 地圖背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A sailor's map, a long argument, the map in your phone, and Taiwan's own grid
culture_cards.title_zh: 水手的地圖、一場爭論、手機裡的地圖，和台灣自己的坐標
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about people choosing what a map should keep.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事，講的都是人怎麼選擇一張地圖要保住什麼。

cards.k: 1569 · For Sailors · 給水手的地圖
cards.body_en: Gerardus Mercator presented his world map in 1569. Part of its long Latin title means “for the use of navigators.” A course that keeps one compass direction is called a rhumb line, and on his map every rhumb line is straight. Sea charts still use the projection today. Its weakness for wall maps was known from the start: the poles cannot be shown at all, and lands far from the equator look far too large.
cards.body_zh: 麥卡托在 1569 年發表他的世界地圖，那一長串拉丁文標題裡有一段的意思是「供航海者使用」。羅盤方向固定不變的航線叫做恆向線，在他的地圖上，每一條恆向線都是直的。今天的海圖仍然使用這種投影。拿來當掛圖的缺點也從一開始就看得出來：兩極根本畫不出來，離赤道遠的陸地看起來大得太多。

cards.k: A Long Argument · 一場爭論
cards.en: Which map belongs on the classroom wall?
cards.zh: 教室牆上該掛哪一張地圖？
cards.body_en: In the 1970s Arno Peters promoted an equal-area map and criticized the Mercator map for making lands far from the equator look too large. In 2017 the public schools of Boston began using a map of this kind. Many mapmakers replied that the Mercator map was designed for navigation, and that the Gall–Peters map bends shapes badly. In 1989 and 1990, seven geographic organizations in North America advised against using any rectangular map as a general world map, and they named both of these. The argument shows that a map is a choice.
cards.body_zh: 1970 年代，彼得斯推廣一種等積地圖，並批評麥卡托地圖把離赤道遠的陸地畫得太大。2017 年，美國波士頓的公立學校開始使用這一類地圖。許多製圖的人則回應：麥卡托地圖是為航海設計的，而高爾－彼得斯地圖把形狀扭曲得很厲害。1989 到 1990 年，北美有七個地理學會與製圖學會建議，一般用途的世界地圖不要用任何長方形的投影，這兩種都點名在內。這場爭論讓人看見：地圖是一種選擇。

cards.k: In Your Pocket · 口袋裡的地圖
cards.zh: 網路地圖為什麼是正方形的
cards.body_en: Most online maps use a form of the Mercator projection, often called Web Mercator. Google's documentation explains that the map is cut off at about 85 degrees north and south, which makes the whole world a square. A square splits neatly into four smaller squares, again and again, and those are the tiles your phone loads as you zoom in. The projection is also good at keeping angles. Zoomed all the way out, it has the same size problem as any Mercator map.
cards.body_zh: 大多數的網路地圖用的是麥卡托投影的一種變化，常被稱為 Web Mercator。Google 的技術文件說明：地圖在南北緯大約 85 度的地方切掉，這樣整個世界剛好是一個正方形。正方形可以整齊地一分為四、再一分為四，這些就是你放大地圖時手機載入的一塊塊圖磚。這種投影也擅長保住角度。把畫面縮到最小時，它和所有的麥卡托地圖一樣，有大小不準的問題。

cards.en: A Mercator map turned on its side
cards.zh: 一張橫過來的麥卡托地圖
cards.body_en: Taiwan's official coordinate system, TWD97, uses a projection called Transverse Mercator. Imagine the Mercator map turned on its side, so that the line of least distortion runs north–south instead of along the equator. Taiwan is a long island running north to south, so this fits it well. According to the National Land Surveying and Mapping Center, the central line for the main island is 121 degrees east, and the zone is only two degrees wide, which keeps the distortion very small.
cards.body_zh: 台灣的官方坐標系統 TWD97，用的是「橫麥卡托投影」。想像把麥卡托地圖橫過來，讓變形最小的那條線不再是赤道，而是一條南北向的線。台灣是一座南北狹長的島，這種投影很適合。依內政部國土測繪中心的說明，台灣本島的中央子午線是東經 121 度，而且一帶只有經度兩度寬（二度分帶），所以變形非常小。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (2018). The elementary-school content has no entry about map projections, so the links below are to junior and senior high school geography.
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年發布）。國小階段的學習內容沒有談地圖投影的條目，所以這裡列的是國中與高中地理。

items.note_en: Latitude and longitude are the grid that every projection moves onto the flat map. Lesson 2 of this series is about that grid.
items.note_zh: 經緯度就是每一種投影搬到平面上的那套格線。本系列第二課會專門談它。

items.area: 社會領域・地理（普通型高中必修）
items.note_en: The curriculum adds a note to this group of entries: “若介紹地圖投影時，應著重於介紹地圖投影的變形及合宜應用的案例。” (If map projections are introduced, the focus should be on their distortion and on cases of fitting use.) That is the idea of this lesson.
items.note_zh: 課綱在這一組條目的說明欄寫：「若介紹地圖投影時，應著重於介紹地圖投影的變形及合宜應用的案例。」這正是本課的主題。

items.area: 社會領域・地理（普通型高中必修）
items.note_en: The game “Which Map Fits the Job?” practices matching a kind of map to a use.
items.note_zh: 「哪一張地圖適合？」這個小遊戲，練習的就是把地圖的種類和用途配起來。

myths.myth_en: The map on the classroom wall shows the true sizes of the lands.
myths.myth_zh: 教室牆上的地圖，畫的就是陸地真正的大小。
myths.fact_en: Only if it is an equal-area map. Many wall maps and almost all online maps enlarge the lands that are far from the equator.
myths.fact_zh: 只有等積地圖才是。很多掛圖和幾乎所有的網路地圖，都把離赤道遠的陸地放大了。

myths.myth_en: The Mercator map is a wrong map, and an equal-area map is the right one.
myths.myth_zh: 麥卡托地圖是錯的地圖，等積地圖才是對的。
myths.fact_en: Each keeps something different. The Mercator map keeps shapes and compass directions. An equal-area map keeps sizes. Each is right for its job and wrong for the other one.
myths.fact_zh: 它們保住的東西不一樣。麥卡托地圖保住形狀和羅盤方向，等積地圖保住大小。各自在自己的用途上是對的，換到對方的用途上就不對。

myths.myth_en: With a good enough computer, someone will make a flat map with no distortion.
myths.myth_zh: 只要電腦夠厲害，總有一天能做出完全沒有變形的平面地圖。
myths.fact_en: This is a matter of geometry, and computing power cannot change it. It was proved about two hundred years ago that a sphere cannot be flattened without distortion. A map can only choose where to put it.
myths.fact_zh: 這是幾何的問題，電腦再厲害也改變不了。大約兩百年前就有人證明：球面不可能毫無變形地攤平。地圖只能選擇把變形放在哪裡。

myths.myth_en: On a map, the shortest way between two places is always a straight line.
myths.myth_zh: 在地圖上，兩地之間最短的路一定是一條直線。
myths.fact_en: On the round Earth, the shortest path follows a great circle. On a Mercator map that path usually looks curved, which is why long flights seem to bend toward the poles.
myths.fact_zh: 在圓的地球上，最短的路沿著大圓走。這條路畫在麥卡托地圖上通常是彎的，所以長途航線看起來會往兩極的方向彎。

tricks.body_en: Remember the tangerine peel. To lie flat, it has to stretch or tear.
tricks.body_zh: 想想橘子皮：要攤平，不是拉扯就是裂開。

tricks.body_en: A flat map can keep some of the four, never all of them.
tricks.body_zh: 一張平面地圖可以保住其中幾樣，不可能四樣全保。

tricks.title_en: Mercator for steering, equal-area for sizes
tricks.title_zh: 要走方向用麥卡托，要比大小用等積
tricks.body_en: One keeps compass directions straight. The other keeps sizes fair.
tricks.body_zh: 一個讓羅盤方向是直線，一個讓大小公平。

tricks.title_en: Ask what the map is for
tricks.title_zh: 先問地圖是做什麼用的
tricks.body_en: There is no best map, only a map that fits the job.
tricks.body_zh: 沒有最好的地圖，只有適合這個用途的地圖。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before the Activities · 做活動之前

safety.en: Peel the fruit with your fingers. If the peel needs a starting cut, an adult makes it. Students do not use knives.
safety.zh: 水果用手剝。如果需要先劃一刀才好剝，由大人來劃；學生不拿刀。

safety.en: Use round-tipped scissors, cut away from your other hand, and pass scissors with the handles toward the other person.
safety.zh: 用圓頭剪刀，剪的時候刀口不要朝向另一隻手；遞剪刀時把握柄朝向對方。

safety.en: Blow up balloons only as far as the teacher shows you, and keep them away from your face when you cut them. Check first whether anyone in the class is allergic to latex.
safety.zh: 氣球只吹到老師示範的大小，剪的時候離臉遠一點。活動前先確認班上有沒有人對乳膠過敏。

safety.en: Wash your hands after handling the fruit, and wipe up juice so that nobody slips.
safety.zh: 碰過水果之後洗手，滴在地上的果汁擦乾，免得有人滑倒。

materials.en: One tangerine or small orange for each pair
materials.zh: 每兩人一顆橘子或小柳丁

materials.en: A marker that writes on the peel
materials.zh: 一支能畫在果皮上的筆

materials.en: A sheet of paper and a heavy book
materials.zh: 一張紙和一本厚書

materials.en: A pencil
materials.zh: 一枝鉛筆

steps.en: Before peeling, draw a line around the middle of the fruit for the equator. Draw four or five circles of the same size on the peel, some near the equator and some near the top.
steps.zh: 剝皮之前，先在水果的腰上畫一圈當赤道。再在果皮上畫四、五個一樣大的圓，有的靠近赤道，有的靠近頂端。

steps.en: Peel the fruit with your fingers, keeping the peel in as few pieces as you can.
steps.zh: 用手把皮剝下來，盡量讓皮保持完整、越少片越好。

steps.en: Lay the peel on the paper with the outside facing up, and press it flat with the book. Watch where it tears.
steps.zh: 把皮攤在紙上、外面朝上，用書壓平。看看它從哪裡裂開。

steps.en: Trace the outline of the flattened peel on the paper. Mark the gaps.
steps.zh: 在紙上描出壓平後果皮的輪廓，把裂縫標出來。

steps.en: Look at your circles. Which ones were torn or pulled out of shape? Compare with the orange-peel map in the 3D model.
steps.zh: 看看你畫的圓，哪些被撕開、被拉得變形了？和 3D 模型裡的「橘子皮地圖」比一比。

activities.tip_en: The peel tears because it cannot stretch. A printed map does not tear because the mapmaker stretches the picture instead. Ask the class: which would you rather have, gaps or stretching?
activities.tip_zh: 果皮會裂開，是因為它不能伸縮。印出來的地圖不會裂開，是因為製圖的人改用「拉扯圖形」來代替。問問全班：你寧願要裂縫，還是要拉扯？

materials.en: One round balloon for each group
materials.zh: 每組一個圓形氣球

materials.en: A permanent marker
materials.zh: 一支油性筆

materials.en: Round-tipped scissors
materials.zh: 圓頭剪刀

materials.en: Four pushpins or pieces of tape, and a piece of cardboard
materials.zh: 四個圖釘或幾段膠帶，和一塊厚紙板

steps.en: Blow the balloon up to the size of a grapefruit and tie it. Draw an equator and six small squares of the same size, some near the equator and some near the knot.
steps.zh: 把氣球吹到葡萄柚那麼大，打結。畫一條赤道，再畫六個一樣大的小正方形，有的靠近赤道，有的靠近打結的地方。

steps.en: Let the air out slowly. Cut the balloon open from the knot to the opposite end.
steps.zh: 慢慢把氣放掉。從打結的地方剪到另一端，把氣球剪開。

steps.en: Stretch the rubber into a rectangle on the cardboard and fix the four corners with tape or pins. An adult helps with the pins.
steps.zh: 把橡皮在厚紙板上拉成長方形，四個角用膠帶或圖釘固定。圖釘請大人幫忙。

steps.en: Measure your squares now. Which ones grew the most? Are they still square?
steps.zh: 現在量一量那些正方形。哪幾個變大最多？還是正方形嗎？

steps.en: Open the 3D model and choose the Mercator map. Do the orange circles change in the same places as your squares?
steps.zh: 打開 3D 模型，選麥卡托地圖。橘色的圓變化的地方，和你的正方形一樣嗎？

activities.tip_en: Rubber can stretch, so the balloon map has no gaps, but the squares near the edge are pulled much bigger than the ones in the middle. That is distortion you can measure with a ruler.
activities.tip_zh: 橡皮可以伸縮，所以氣球地圖沒有裂縫；但靠邊的正方形被拉得比中間的大很多。這就是可以用尺量出來的變形。

links_head.en: The round Earth in other lessons, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 其他課裡的圓形地球，以及下一課

links.en: Why Do We Have Seasons?
links.zh: 為什麼有四季？
links.note_en: The same round, tilted Earth, seen from space. That lesson shows why sunlight falls differently at different latitudes.
links.note_zh: 同一顆圓圓的、歪著轉的地球，從太空看。那一課說明為什麼不同緯度照到的陽光不一樣。

links.en: How Does GPS Know Where You Are?
links.zh: GPS 怎麼知道你在哪裡？
links.note_en: Satellites find your position on the round Earth. A map projection then decides where that position lands on your flat screen.
links.note_zh: 衛星先在圓的地球上找出你的位置，地圖投影再決定這個位置要畫在平面螢幕的哪裡。

links.en: How Do You Find Any Place on Earth?
links.zh: 怎麼找到地球上任何一個地方？
links.note_en: Latitude and longitude: two numbers that work like an address for any spot on the globe.
links.note_zh: 經度和緯度：兩個數字，就是地球上任何一個地方的地址。

sources.en: A map projection is “a systematic representation of all or part of the surface of a round body, especially the Earth, on a plane”; this “cannot be done without distortion.” Formulas for the projections, the scale factor sec φ of the Mercator projection, and Tissot's analysis of distortion (1859, 1881).
sources.zh: 地圖投影的定義、「不可能沒有變形」、各投影的公式、麥卡托的比例因子 sec φ、底索的變形分析（1859、1881）
sources.src: Snyder, Map Projections: A Working Manual, USGS Professional Paper 1395 (1987)

sources.en: Mercator projection: presented in 1569; conformal; rhumb lines are straight; the poles cannot be shown; the 1569 title includes “ad usum navigantium.” Plate carrée credited to Marinus of Tyre, about AD 100; Mollweide presented in 1805; Gall's projection, 1855.
sources.zh: 麥卡托投影：1569 年發表、正形、恆向線是直線、畫不到極點、標題有「供航海者使用」；等距圓柱投影約西元 100 年；莫爾威投影 1805 年；高爾的投影 1855 年
sources.src: Snyder (1987), chapters 7, 10, 12, 31

sources.en: “Any straight line on a Mercator projection map is a line of constant true bearing”; introduced in 1569 by Gerardus Mercator; areas farther from the equator appear disproportionately large.
sources.zh: 麥卡托地圖上的直線是方位固定的線；1569 年由麥卡托提出；離赤道越遠的地區看起來越大
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Mercator projection”

sources.en: “All projections involve some degree of distortion.”
sources.zh: 所有的投影都有某種程度的變形
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “projection (cartography)”

sources.en: Gauss's Theorema Egregium (1827): the surface of a sphere cannot be unfolded onto a plane without distorting distances.
sources.zh: 高斯的「絕妙定理」（1827 年）：球面不可能攤成平面而不改變距離
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Theorema Egregium”

sources.en: Area of Greenland: 2,166,086 km².

lessons.title: How Do You Find Any Place on Earth?
lessons.title_zh: 怎麼找到地球上任何一個地方？
lessons.blurb_en: Drag a point around a 3D globe and read its latitude and longitude. See the two angles from the center of the Earth, find eight places from their numbers, and learn why one degree is not always the same distance.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 地球儀上拖動一個點，讀出它的緯度和經度。看看從地心量出來的兩個角，照著數字找出八個地方，再想想為什麼「一度」不一定一樣長。
lessons.big_idea_en: Two numbers work like an address for any spot on Earth. Latitude tells how far north or south of the equator it is. Longitude tells how far east or west of the prime meridian it is. Both numbers are angles.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 兩個數字，就是地球上任何一個地方的地址。緯度說它在赤道的北邊或南邊多遠，經度說它在本初子午線的東邊或西邊多遠。這兩個數字都是角度。

paras: Imagine a ship far out in the middle of the ocean. There are no streets, no signs, and no buildings, only water in every direction. If the ship needs help, how can the sailors tell anyone where they are? On land we use addresses with street names and house numbers. The ocean has none of these. Luckily, the whole Earth has an address system of its own, and it needs only two numbers.

The first number is latitude. Picture a line around the middle of the Earth, halfway between the North Pole and the South Pole. This is the equator. Latitude tells you how far north or south of the equator a place is. It is measured in degrees, from 0 at the equator to 90 at each pole. Lines of latitude are circles that run east and west. They are also called parallels, because they never meet, and they get smaller as they get closer to the poles.

The second number is longitude. Lines of longitude, also called meridians, run from the North Pole to the South Pole. One of them is chosen as the starting line and is called the prime meridian. It passes through Greenwich, in London. Longitude tells you how far east or west of the prime meridian a place is, from 0 degrees up to 180 degrees. Unlike lines of latitude, all lines of longitude meet at the two poles.

Put the two numbers together and you have an address. Latitude is said first, then longitude. The middle of Taiwan is at about 23.5 degrees north, 121 degrees east. For more exact work, each degree is divided into 60 smaller parts called minutes. One degree of latitude is about 111 kilometers on the ground wherever you are. One degree of longitude is about 111 kilometers at the equator, but it shrinks toward the poles, where all the lines come together.

Why does longitude start at Greenwich? The equator is set by the way the Earth spins, so nobody had to choose it. The prime meridian is different. Any line from pole to pole could have been the starting line, and for a long time different countries used different ones. In 1884, delegates from 25 countries met in Washington, D.C., and voted to use the line through the observatory at Greenwich, which most ships' charts already used. The prime meridian is an agreement among people.

For sailors, latitude was the easy number. In the Northern Hemisphere, the height of the North Star above the horizon is about the same as your latitude. Longitude was much harder, because finding it means knowing the exact time. The Earth turns 15 degrees every hour, so a clock that keeps the time of a known place can tell a ship how far east or west it has sailed. In the 1700s, the English clockmaker John Harrison built clocks that could do this at sea. Today the satellites of GPS give your phone both numbers in a few seconds.
paras_zh: 想像一艘船在大海的正中央。沒有街道、沒有路牌、沒有建築，四面八方只有海水。如果這艘船需要幫忙，船上的人要怎麼告訴別人自己在哪裡？在陸地上，我們用有路名和門牌號碼的地址；大海上這些都沒有。還好，整個地球有一套自己的地址系統，而且只需要兩個數字。
第一個數字是緯度。想像有一條線繞著地球的腰，剛好在北極和南極的正中間，這就是赤道。緯度告訴你一個地方在赤道的北邊或南邊多遠。它用「度」來量，赤道是 0 度，兩極各是 90 度。緯線是東西向的圓圈。它們彼此平行、永遠不會相交，而且越靠近兩極，圓圈就越小。
第二個數字是經度。經線（英文是 lines of longitude，也叫 meridians）從北極一路畫到南極。其中有一條被選為起點，叫做本初子午線，它通過倫敦的格林威治。經度告訴你一個地方在本初子午線的東邊或西邊多遠，從 0 度到 180 度。和緯線不一樣的是，所有的經線都在南北兩極會合。
把兩個數字放在一起，就是一個地址。先說緯度，再說經度。台灣的中間大約在北緯 23.5 度、東經 121 度。需要更精確的時候，每一度再分成 60 個更小的單位，叫做「分」。一度緯度在地面上大約是 111 公里，到哪裡都差不多。一度經度在赤道上也大約是 111 公里，但越往兩極越短，因為所有的經線在那裡聚在一起。
經度為什麼從格林威治算起？赤道是地球自轉的方式決定的，不需要誰來選。本初子午線就不一樣了：任何一條從北極到南極的線都可以當起點，而且有很長一段時間，各國用的起點都不一樣。1884 年，25 個國家的代表在美國華盛頓開會，表決採用通過格林威治天文台的那一條線——當時大多數船隻用的海圖，本來就以它為準。本初子午線是人和人之間的約定。
對航海的人來說，緯度是比較容易的那個數字。在北半球，北極星在地平線上的高度，大約就等於你所在的緯度。經度難得多，因為要知道經度，就得知道準確的時間。地球每小時轉 15 度，所以只要有一個鐘一直保持某個已知地點的時間，就能算出船往東或往西走了多遠。十八世紀，英國的鐘錶匠哈里森做出了能在海上辦到這件事的鐘。今天，GPS 衛星幾秒鐘就能把這兩個數字送到你的手機上。
questions: Lines of latitude are called parallels. Why does that name not fit lines of longitude?
Why did people have to hold a meeting to choose the prime meridian, but not the equator?
A place is at 60 degrees north. You walk along its line of latitude until your longitude has changed by one degree. Did you walk more or less than 111 kilometers? Why?
answers: Parallel lines never meet. Lines of latitude never meet, but all lines of longitude come together at the North Pole and the South Pole, so they are not parallel.

The equator is fixed by the Earth's spin: it is the circle halfway between the two poles. No line of longitude is special in that way, so people had to agree on which one would be zero. In 1884 they agreed on the line through Greenwich.
Less. Lines of longitude get closer together toward the poles. At 60 degrees north, one degree of longitude is only half as long as at the equator, about 56 kilometers.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: The dot climbs north from the equator along one line of longitude. Watch the gold wedge at the center of the Earth open: that angle is the latitude.
parts.text_zh: 那個點沿著同一條經線，從赤道往北爬。看地心那片金色的扇形慢慢張開：那個角就是緯度。

parts.text_en: The dot slides east along the equator, starting from the prime meridian. The blue wedge opens in the flat plane of the equator: that angle is the longitude.
parts.text_zh: 那個點從本初子午線出發，沿著赤道往東滑。藍色的扇形在赤道的平面上張開：那個角就是經度。

parts.meta_zh: 北緯 23.7 度、東經 121 度
parts.text_en: Fly to Taiwan and see both wedges at once. The gold one says how far north of the equator. The blue one says how far east of Greenwich.
parts.text_zh: 飛到台灣，同時看到兩片扇形。金色的說它在赤道以北多遠，藍色的說它在格林威治以東多遠。

parts.text_en: Send the dot to the North Pole. Its line of latitude shrinks to a single point, every line of longitude meets there, and the longitude reading disappears.
parts.text_zh: 把那個點送到北極。它的緯線縮成一個點，所有的經線都在那裡會合，經度的讀數也不見了。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Can you put the dot on a place that is in the Southern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere at the same time?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。你能把那個點放在一個同時屬於南半球和西半球的地方嗎？

find.lead_en: Eight places. Each one is given only as two numbers. Click where you think it is on the map. If you miss, the game tells you which way to move. There is no timer, and the game counts the places you find on the first try.

find.start_en: Find the line of latitude first, then follow it east or west to the longitude.

find.end_en: With two numbers you can point to any spot on Earth, on land or in the middle of the sea.
find.end_zh: 有了兩個數字，就能指出地球上任何一個地方，不管在陸地上還是大海中間。

degree.lead_en: A degree is an angle, and its length on the ground depends on the direction. Slide the latitude from the equator to the pole. The gold box is one degree of latitude tall and one degree of longitude wide, drawn to scale. The numbers treat the Earth as a perfect ball with a radius of 6,371 km; the real Earth is slightly flattened, so real values differ by less than one percent.
degree.lead_zh: 「度」是角度，它在地面上有多長，要看是哪個方向。把緯度從赤道拉到極點看看。金色的格子高是一度緯度、寬是一度經度，照比例畫。這裡把地球當成半徑 6,371 公里的正圓球來算；真正的地球稍微扁一點，所以實際的數字會差不到百分之一。

degree.msg_mid_en: The box keeps its height and loses its width. One degree of latitude stays about 111 km; one degree of longitude is 111 km times the cosine of the latitude.

degree.msg_half_en: At 60 degrees, one degree of longitude is exactly half as long as at the equator.

degree.msg_pole_en: At the pole the box has no width at all. You could walk through all 360 degrees of longitude in a few steps.

culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people drew lines on the Earth and agreed on them.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事，講人怎麼在地球上畫線，又怎麼取得共識。

cards.body_en: In October 1884, 41 delegates from 25 countries met in Washington, D.C., to choose one starting line for longitude. The vote for Greenwich was 22 in favor and 1 against, with 2 countries not voting. According to the Royal Observatory, Greenwich was chosen because it caused the least disruption: nearly two-thirds of the world's ships already used charts based on it. The same meeting agreed to count longitude in two directions, up to 180 degrees east and 180 degrees west.
cards.body_zh: 1884 年 10 月，25 個國家的 41 位代表在美國華盛頓開會，要選出一條共同的經度起點。表決結果是 22 票贊成格林威治、1 票反對，另有 2 國棄權。依格林威治皇家天文台的說明，選它是因為造成的變動最小：當時全世界將近三分之二的船，用的海圖本來就以它為準。同一場會議也決定，經度往東、往西兩個方向各算到 180 度。

cards.body_en: The Earth turns 360 degrees in 24 hours, which is 15 degrees every hour. So if a ship carries a clock set to the time of a known place, each hour of difference from local noon means 15 degrees of longitude. The hard part was building a clock that stayed accurate on a rolling ship. In 1714 the British Parliament passed the Longitude Act, offering rewards of up to 20,000 pounds for a solution. John Harrison completed his sea watch, now called H4, in 1759. It was tested on a voyage to Jamaica that began in 1761, and again on a voyage to Barbados in 1764.
cards.body_zh: 地球 24 小時轉 360 度，也就是每小時 15 度。所以只要船上有一個鐘，一直保持某個已知地點的時間，它和當地正午每差一小時，就是 15 度的經度。難的是做出一個在搖晃的船上還走得準的鐘。1714 年，英國國會通過《經度法案》，懸賞最高兩萬英鎊徵求解法。哈里森在 1759 年完成他的航海鐘（今天稱為 H4），1761 年起在前往牙買加的航程中測試，1764 年又在前往巴貝多的航程中再測一次。

cards.en: A line that crosses the island, and moves
cards.zh: 一條穿過台灣、還會移動的線
cards.body_en: The Tropic of Cancer, at about 23.5 degrees north, runs across Taiwan. Taiwan's Tourism Administration lists three markers on the main island: in Shuishang Township in Chiayi County, on the Wuhe Terrace in Ruisui Township in Hualien County, and in Fengbin Township in Hualien County. At noon on the June solstice the Sun is straight overhead on this line, and a pole standing upright casts no shadow. The line is not fixed. It is drifting south by a little more than 14 meters a year, and in 1788 it ran through what is now a street corner in Chiayi City.
cards.body_zh: 北回歸線大約在北緯 23.5 度，橫貫台灣。交通部觀光署的資料列出本島的三座北回歸線標：嘉義縣水上鄉、花蓮縣瑞穗鄉舞鶴台地、花蓮縣豐濱鄉。每年夏至正午，太陽直射這條線，可以看到「立竿不見影」。這條線並不是固定的：它平均每年以 14 公尺多的速度往南移，1788 年時通過的地方，是今天嘉義市的一個路口。

cards.en: The line at Greenwich has moved 102 meters
cards.zh: 格林威治那條線，移了 102 公尺
cards.body_en: Visitors to Greenwich like to stand on the brass line that marks the historic prime meridian, with one foot in the east and one in the west. But a phone standing on that line does not read exactly zero. Satellite navigation uses a newer reference line, which passes 102.5 meters to the east of the old one. The old line was set by a telescope on the ground; the new one comes from measurements of the whole Earth. A degree of longitude is still a degree, counted from a slightly different zero.
cards.body_zh: 到格林威治的遊客，喜歡站在標示舊本初子午線的那條銅線上，一腳在東、一腳在西。但把手機放在那條線上，讀數並不會剛好是 0。衛星導航用的是一條比較新的參考線，在舊線東邊 102.5 公尺的地方。舊線是用地面上的一架望遠鏡定出來的，新線則來自對整個地球的測量。經度的「度」還是一樣的度，只是零點稍微挪了一點。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: This entry comes from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (2018). The curriculum writes the word for “coordinate” as 座標; surveying agencies in Taiwan write 坐標. We quote each as it is written.
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年發布）。課綱寫「座標」，國土測繪機關寫「坐標」；本教材引用時各照原文。

items.note_en: This lesson is a first look at that system: what the two numbers mean, where they start, and how to read and say them.
items.note_zh: 這一課就是這套系統的入門：兩個數字各代表什麼、從哪裡算起、怎麼讀和怎麼說。

myths.myth_en: A degree is a fixed distance, like a kilometer.
myths.myth_zh: 「一度」是固定的距離，就像一公里一樣。
myths.fact_en: A degree is an angle. One degree of latitude is about 111 km everywhere, but one degree of longitude is about 111 km at the equator, about 56 km at 60 degrees, and nothing at the poles.
myths.fact_zh: 「度」是角度。一度緯度到哪裡都大約是 111 公里；一度經度在赤道約 111 公里，在緯度 60 度約 56 公里，到了兩極是 0。

myths.myth_en: The prime meridian is a natural line, just like the equator.
myths.myth_zh: 本初子午線和赤道一樣，是自然形成的線。
myths.fact_en: The equator is set by the Earth's spin. The prime meridian is an agreement: it was chosen by a vote at an international conference in 1884.
myths.fact_zh: 赤道是地球自轉決定的。本初子午線則是約定：它是 1884 年一場國際會議表決選出來的。

myths.myth_en: Lines of longitude are parallel to each other, like lines of latitude.
myths.myth_zh: 經線彼此平行，就像緯線一樣。
myths.fact_en: Lines of latitude are parallel and never meet. Lines of longitude are farthest apart at the equator and all meet at the poles.
myths.fact_zh: 緯線彼此平行、永遠不相交。經線在赤道上隔得最開，到了兩極全部會合。

myths.myth_en: If you stand on the line at Greenwich, your phone will show a longitude of exactly zero.
myths.myth_zh: 站在格林威治的那條線上，手機顯示的經度會剛好是 0。
myths.fact_en: Satellite navigation counts longitude from a newer line about 102 meters to the east, so on the historic line a phone shows a tiny bit of west longitude.
myths.fact_zh: 衛星導航的經度是從東邊大約 102 公尺的一條新線算起的，所以站在舊線上，手機會顯示一點點西經。

tricks_head.en: Latitude and longitude in a sentence

tricks.body_en: The lines lie flat, one above another, and you climb them to go north.
tricks.body_zh: 一條一條橫著排上去；往北走，就像往上爬。

tricks.body_en: Every one runs the long way, from pole to pole, and they are all the same length.
tricks.body_zh: 每一條都從北極拉到南極，而且每一條都一樣長。

tricks.body_en: The same order as in the dictionary: “la” comes before “lo.”
tricks.body_zh: 和字典的順序一樣：la 排在 lo 前面。

tricks.title_en: N and S for latitude, E and W for longitude
tricks.title_zh: 緯度配南北，經度配東西
tricks.body_en: A latitude can never be more than 90. A longitude can go up to 180.
tricks.body_zh: 緯度最多 90，經度最多 180。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before the Activities · 做活動之前

safety.en: Stretch rubber bands only as far as they need to go, and never aim one at another person. A band that snaps can hurt an eye.
safety.zh: 橡皮筋只拉到需要的長度，絕對不要對著別人。橡皮筋彈開可能傷到眼睛。

safety.en: Use washable markers on the ball or fruit, and wash your hands before eating anything.
safety.zh: 在球或水果上畫線用水性筆；吃東西之前先洗手。

safety.en: If you go outside at night to look for the North Star, go with an adult, stay away from roads, and take a flashlight.
safety.zh: 晚上到戶外找北極星時，要有大人陪同、遠離馬路，並帶手電筒。

safety.en: Never look at the Sun, even to find a direction.
safety.zh: 絕對不要直視太陽，即使只是為了找方向。

materials.en: A ball about the size of a grapefruit, or an orange
materials.zh: 一顆葡萄柚大小的球，或一顆柳丁

materials.en: Six rubber bands in two colors
materials.zh: 六條橡皮筋，兩種顏色

materials.en: A washable marker and two small stickers
materials.zh: 一支水性筆和兩張小貼紙

materials.en: A globe or world map to check against
materials.zh: 一顆地球儀或一張世界地圖，用來對照

steps.en: Put the two stickers on opposite sides of the ball. These are the North Pole and the South Pole.
steps.zh: 把兩張貼紙貼在球的正對面兩側，當作北極和南極。

steps.en: Stretch one band around the middle, halfway between the poles. This is the equator, 0 degrees latitude.
steps.zh: 把一條橡皮筋套在球的腰上，剛好在兩極的正中間。這是赤道，緯度 0 度。

steps.en: Stretch three bands of the other color so that each one passes over both poles. Space them evenly. You have made six half-circles of longitude, 60 degrees apart. Mark one of them with the marker as the prime meridian.
steps.zh: 用另一種顏色的三條橡皮筋，每一條都繞過兩極，間隔平均。這樣就有六條半圓形的經線，彼此相隔 60 度。用筆把其中一條標成本初子午線。

steps.en: Try to add a band for 60 degrees north. Notice that it has to be a much smaller circle than the equator, and that it will not stay on unless the ball is a little rough.
steps.zh: 試著再加一條北緯 60 度的橡皮筋。你會發現它得是一個比赤道小很多的圓，而且除非球面有點粗糙，否則很難固定。

steps.en: Find where Taiwan belongs: about a quarter of the way from the equator to the North Pole, and one-third of the way around the ball to the east of your prime meridian. Mark it with a dot.
steps.zh: 找出台灣該在的位置：從赤道到北極大約四分之一的地方，從本初子午線往東繞大約三分之一圈。點一個點。

activities.tip_en: Ask the class: which bands are all the same length, and which are not? The longitude bands are all the same. The latitude bands get shorter toward the poles. That is why one degree of longitude shrinks.
activities.tip_zh: 問問全班：哪些橡皮筋一樣長，哪些不一樣？經線那幾條都一樣長；緯線那幾條越靠近兩極越短。這就是一度經度會變短的原因。

materials.en: A printed world map with latitude and longitude lines every 30 degrees, one for each pair
materials.zh: 每兩人一張印好的世界地圖，上面每 30 度有一條經緯線

materials.en: Ten small counters or paper dots for each pair
materials.zh: 每組十個小圓片或小紙點

materials.en: A folder to stand between the two partners
materials.zh: 一個可以立在兩人中間的資料夾

steps.en: Partner A secretly places five counters on the map, each where two grid lines cross.
steps.zh: 甲同學偷偷把五個圓片放在地圖上，每一個都放在兩條格線的交點。

steps.en: Partner A reads each position aloud in English, latitude first: “thirty degrees north, one hundred twenty degrees east.”
steps.zh: 甲同學用英文把每個位置唸出來，先說緯度：「thirty degrees north, one hundred twenty degrees east.」

steps.en: Partner B listens and places a counter on the same crossing on a second map.
steps.zh: 乙同學邊聽邊在另一張地圖的同一個交點放上圓片。

steps.en: Remove the folder and compare the two maps. Score one point for each counter in the right place.
steps.zh: 把資料夾拿開，比對兩張地圖。每放對一個圓片得一分。

steps.en: Swap roles. For a harder round, place counters halfway between the lines and say “about fifteen degrees south.”
steps.zh: 交換角色。想難一點，就把圓片放在兩條線的中間，說「about fifteen degrees south」。

activities.tip_en: The most common mistake is swapping the two numbers. Remind students that a latitude can never be more than 90, so “one hundred twenty degrees north” cannot exist.
activities.tip_zh: 最常見的錯誤是把兩個數字說反。提醒學生：緯度不可能超過 90，所以不會有「北緯 120 度」。

lessons.title: How Do You Draw a Mountain on Flat Paper?
lessons.title_zh: 怎麼在平面上畫出一座山？
lessons.blurb_en: Fill a tank around a mountain with water, one step at a time, and let the water's edge draw contour lines. Then look from above, read which slopes are steep, and turn any line on the map into a side view.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在一座山的四周一層一層灌水，讓水邊畫出等高線。再從正上方看、判斷哪裡陡，把地圖上任何一條線變成側面圖。
lessons.big_idea_en: A contour line joins points that are the same height above sea level. Draw one every few meters of height and a flat map can show a mountain: where the lines crowd together, the slope is steep, and where they spread apart, it is gentle.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 等高線把海拔一樣高的點連起來。每隔固定的高度畫一條，平面的地圖就能畫出一座山：線擠在一起的地方坡很陡，線分得很開的地方坡很緩。

lab.title_en: A Mountain in a Tank of Water
lab.how_en: Press “Raise the water,” or drag the slider. Each time the water climbs one contour interval, its edge leaves a gold line on the mountain. When the summit is under water, switch to “From above”: the lines you see are a contour map. Click anywhere on the mountain to read its height and slope. This is an imaginary island, not a real place.
lab.how_zh: 按「升高水位」，或拖動滑桿。水每升高一個等高距，水邊就在山上留下一條金色的線。等山頂也淹沒了，切到「從正上方看」：你看到的那些線，就是一張等高線地圖。點山上任何一個地方，可以讀出它的海拔和坡度。這是一座想像的島，不是真實的地方。

lab.scale_en: The island is 10 km across and its summit is about 1,000 m high. Heights in the model are drawn 1.5 times taller than they really are, so the shape is easier to see.
lab.scale_zh: 這座島寬 10 公里，山頂大約 1,000 公尺。模型裡的高度畫成實際的 1.5 倍，讓形狀比較容易看清楚。
lab.credit_html: The island is an imaginary landform made by the page itself from a mathematical formula, so that every height and slope can be computed and tested. · 這座島是頁面用數學式自己做出來的想像地形，所以每一個高度和坡度都算得出來、也有自動測試。

paras: A map is flat, but the land is not. Some places are high and some are low, and a hiker, a farmer, or a person choosing where to build a house needs to know which is which. How can a flat sheet of paper show a mountain? One clever answer is the contour line.

A contour line joins points that are the same height above sea level. Imagine an island in the middle of a calm sea. The edge of the water traces a line all the way around the island, and every point on that line is at a height of zero. That line is the coastline, and it is also the first contour line.

Now imagine that the sea rises by 100 meters. The water's edge moves up the mountain and traces a new, shorter loop. Every point on it is 100 meters high. Let the water rise another 100 meters, and another, and each time draw the new edge. When you look down from above, you see rings inside rings. The difference in height between one line and the next is called the contour interval.

The spacing of the lines tells you the shape of the land. Where the lines crowd together, the ground rises quickly over a short distance, so the slope is steep. Where the lines are far apart, the ground rises slowly, and the slope is gentle. A small closed ring in the middle marks a summit. Two summits with a low dip between them make a saddle, and lines that bend into a V show a valley.

Mapmakers make contour maps easier to read in a few ways. Every fourth or fifth line is usually drawn thicker and labeled with its height, so you do not have to count all the lines. Many maps also color the land by height. The height of a mountain is measured from sea level, so countries choose an official starting point. Taiwan's heights are measured from the average sea level at the tide station in Keelung.

With practice, you can read a contour map like a picture. You can tell which path to the top is shorter but steeper, where a river will flow, and what you would see if you cut the mountain in half and looked at it from the side. That side view is called a profile. Contour lines turn the ups and downs of the land into lines that a flat map can hold.
paras_zh: 地圖是平的，土地卻不是。有些地方高、有些地方低，登山的人、種田的人、要選地方蓋房子的人，都得知道哪裡高、哪裡低。一張平平的紙，要怎麼畫出一座山？有一個很聰明的答案：等高線。
等高線把海拔一樣高的點連起來。想像大海中間有一座島，海面很平靜。水邊沿著島繞了一整圈，這條線上的每一個點，高度都是 0。這條線就是海岸線，也是第一條等高線。
現在想像海面升高 100 公尺。水邊往山上移，畫出一圈新的、比較短的線，線上每一點都是 100 公尺高。再升高 100 公尺、再升高 100 公尺，每次都把新的水邊畫下來。從正上方往下看，你會看到一圈套著一圈。相鄰兩條線之間的高度差，叫做等高距。
線和線之間的距離，告訴你土地的形狀。線擠在一起的地方，很短的距離裡地面就升得很高，所以坡很陡；線分得很開的地方，地面升得很慢，坡就很緩。中間一個小小的封閉圓圈是山頂。兩座山頂中間低下去的地方是鞍部，彎成 V 字形的線代表山谷。
製圖的人用幾種方法讓等高線地圖更好讀。通常每四條或五條線就有一條畫得比較粗，並標上高度，不用一條一條數。很多地圖也會照高度幫陸地上色。山的高度是從海平面量起的，所以每個國家都要選一個官方的起點；台灣的高度，是從基隆潮位站量到的平均海平面算起。
多練習幾次，你就能把等高線地圖當成一幅畫來讀。你看得出哪一條上山的路比較短、但比較陡，河會往哪裡流，以及把山從中間切開、從側面看會是什麼樣子。這個側面的樣子叫做剖面。等高線把土地的高高低低，變成了平面地圖裝得下的線。
questions: Why is the coastline also a contour line?
On a contour map, two paths lead to the same summit. One crosses many lines that are close together. The other crosses the same lines, but they are far apart. Which path is steeper, and why?
Why do contour lines of different heights never cross each other on a normal map?
answers: Every point on the coastline is at the same height: sea level, 0 meters. A contour line joins points of the same height, so the coastline is the 0 m contour line.
The path across the crowded lines is steeper. It climbs the same height in a shorter distance.
One spot on the ground has only one height. If two lines of different heights crossed, the crossing point would need two different heights at once, which is impossible.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Watch the water rise from sea level to the summit. Each time it climbs 100 m, its edge leaves a gold line on the mountain. The U.S. Geological Survey explains contour lines with this same picture of a rising sea.
parts.text_zh: 看水從海平面一路升到山頂。每升高 100 公尺，水邊就在山上留下一條金色的線。美國地質調查所（USGS）解說等高線時，用的也是「海面升高」這個畫面。

parts.en: From above, it is a map
parts.text_en: The camera moves straight overhead. The rings you see are exactly what a contour map shows.
parts.text_zh: 鏡頭移到正上方。你看到的一圈一圈，就是等高線地圖畫的東西。

parts.text_en: On the east side the lines crowd together. The marked spot there has a slope of more than 30 degrees. Compare it with the west side, where the lines spread out.
parts.text_zh: 東邊的線擠在一起，那裡標出的點坡度超過 30 度。和西邊線分得很開的地方比一比。

parts.text_en: The water stops just above the low point between the two peaks. A little higher and the two islands would be separate. That low point is the saddle.
parts.text_zh: 水停在兩座山之間最低點的上方一點。再高一點，就會變成兩座分開的島。那個最低點就是鞍部。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself. Change the contour interval to 50 m and to 200 m. Which one shows the shape best, and which one is easiest to read?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後自己動手試試。把等高距改成 50 公尺和 200 公尺。哪一種最能看出山的形狀？哪一種最好讀？

steep.lead_en: Eight questions about the same island. Read the contour map and choose path A or path B. After you answer, the side views of both paths appear, drawn to the same scale, so you can check. There is no timer, and the game counts the questions you get right on the first try.
steep.lead_zh: 同一座島的八個問題。讀等高線地圖，選路線 A 或 B。答完以後，兩條路線的側面會照同樣的比例畫出來，讓你對答案。不計時，遊戲會記下你第一次就答對的題數。
steep.start_en: Count how many lines each path crosses, and look at how close together they are.
steep.start_zh: 數一數每條路線穿過幾條線，再看看那些線擠得多近。
steep.end_en: Close lines mean a steep climb; far-apart lines mean an easy one. Now you can read a mountain from a flat map.
steep.end_zh: 線擠在一起就是陡坡，線分得開就是緩坡。現在你能從一張平面地圖讀出一座山了。

steeper.en: Steeper means more height in less distance. Look for the path where the lines are closest together.
steeper.zh: 比較陡，就是在比較短的距離裡升得比較高。找線擠得最近的那一條。

easier.en: An easier walk climbs slowly. Look for the path where the lines are far apart.
easier.zh: 好走的路升得慢。找線分得最開的那一條。

higher.en: Look for the highest numbered line, or the innermost ring, that each path reaches.
higher.zh: 看每條路線碰到的最高那條線（標的數字最大、或最裡面的那一圈）。

climb.en: Count the lines each path crosses on the way up. Every line is another 100 m of climbing.
climb.zh: 數每條路線往上走時穿過幾條線。每多一條，就要多爬 100 公尺。

questions.en: Both paths end at the summit. Which one is steeper?
questions.zh: 兩條路線都到山頂。哪一條比較陡？
questions.why_en: Path A climbs about the same height in a much shorter distance. Its lines are crowded together.
questions.why_zh: A 路線爬差不多的高度，走的距離卻短得多；它經過的線擠在一起。

questions.en: You are carrying a heavy pack. Which path is the easier climb?
questions.zh: 你背著很重的背包。哪一條路比較好爬？
questions.why_en: Path A crosses lines that are spread out, so it rises more slowly.
questions.why_zh: A 路線經過的線分得比較開，所以升得比較慢。

questions.en: Both paths cross the island. Which one goes higher?
questions.zh: 兩條路線都橫越這座島。哪一條走得比較高？
questions.why_en: Path A passes right by the summit. Path B crosses through the low saddle between the peaks.
questions.why_zh: A 路線從山頂旁邊經過；B 路線從兩座山之間低低的鞍部穿過去。

questions.en: Which path makes you climb more meters in total?
questions.zh: 哪一條路線總共要爬比較多公尺？
questions.why_en: Path B goes all the way to the summit, about 1,000 m. Path A follows the valley and stops near 200 m.
questions.why_zh: B 路線一路爬到山頂，大約 1,000 公尺；A 路線沿著山谷走，到 200 公尺左右就停了。

questions.en: Which path is steeper?
questions.zh: 哪一條路線比較陡？
questions.why_en: Path B is short and crosses many crowded lines on the east face of the main peak.
questions.why_zh: B 路線很短，卻穿過主峰東坡上很多擠在一起的線。

questions.en: Which path reaches a higher point?
questions.zh: 哪一條路線會經過比較高的地方？
questions.why_en: Path A climbs over the shoulder of the main peak. Path B stays low in the valley.
questions.why_zh: A 路線翻過主峰的山肩；B 路線一直待在低低的山谷裡。

questions.en: Which path is the easier climb?
questions.zh: 哪一條路比較好爬？
questions.why_en: Path A goes up the lower peak, where the lines are farther apart. Path B goes up the steep east face of the main peak.
questions.why_zh: A 路線爬的是比較矮、線比較開的副峰；B 路線爬的是主峰陡峭的東坡。

questions.en: Which path makes you climb more meters in total?
questions.zh: 哪一條路線總共要爬比較多公尺？
questions.why_en: Path B reaches the top of the lower peak, about 540 m. Path A stays in the valley and climbs only about 260 m.
questions.why_zh: B 路線爬到副峰頂，大約 540 公尺；A 路線待在山谷裡，只爬大約 260 公尺。

profile.en: From Contour Lines to a Side View
profile.lead_en: Drag the ends of the pink line, A and B, anywhere on the map. The side view shows the land along the line, as if you had cut the island with a knife and looked at the cut. Notice how the crowded lines on the map turn into steep slopes in the side view.
profile.lead_zh: 把粉紅色線的兩端 A、B 拖到地圖上任何地方。側面圖畫的是沿著這條線的地面，就像拿刀把島切開、看切開的那一面。注意地圖上擠在一起的線，到了側面圖就變成陡坡。

map_english.en: Eight sentences for talking about high and low
map_english.zh: 說高低與坡度的八句英文
map_english.lead_en: This lesson's Map English card is about height and slope. Listen, repeat, then describe the island in the model to a partner.
map_english.lead_zh: 這一課的「地圖英語」練習說高低和坡度。先聽、再跟著唸，然後對著模型裡的島，向同伴描述它的樣子。

items.en: The summit is about one thousand meters above sea level.
items.zh: 山頂大約海拔一千公尺。
items.use_en: … meters above sea level: for elevation

items.en: The contour lines are close together on the east side.
items.zh: 東邊的等高線擠在一起。

items.en: The slope is steep, so the path zigzags.
items.zh: 坡很陡，所以小路走之字形。

items.en: The river flows down the valley to the sea.
items.zh: 河沿著山谷往下流到海裡。

items.en: There is a saddle between the two peaks.
items.zh: 兩座山峰之間有一個鞍部。
items.use_zh: 在 A 和 B 之間

items.en: The contour interval on this map is one hundred meters.
items.zh: 這張地圖的等高距是一百公尺。
items.use_zh: 說地圖本身的規格用 on this map

items.en: We climbed four hundred meters in two kilometers.
items.zh: 我們走兩公里，爬升了四百公尺。

items.en: If you cut the mountain in half, you can see its profile.
items.zh: 把山從中間切開，就能看到它的剖面。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Lines · 線背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Lines under the water, lines on the land, Taiwan's maps, and the height of Yushan
culture_cards.title_zh: 水下的線、陸上的線、台灣的地形圖，和玉山的高度
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people learned to draw height on paper and how they measure it.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事，講人怎麼學會把高度畫到紙上，又怎麼量高度。

cards.body_en: Some of the first lines of equal height were really lines of equal depth, drawn for boats. Around 1729 and 1730, the Dutch engineer Nicolaas Cruquius published a map of the river Merwede that, according to Utrecht University Library, was the first to use a printed system of depth contours. A few years later the French geographer Philippe Buache drew depth lines on a chart of the English Channel, prepared in 1737 and published in 1752.
cards.body_zh: 最早的一些「等高線」其實是「等深線」，是為了行船畫的。大約 1729 到 1730 年，荷蘭工程師克魯奎烏斯出版了一張默韋德河的地圖；依荷蘭烏特勒支大學圖書館的說明，這是第一張用印刷的等深線系統畫成的地圖。幾年後，法國地理學家布阿許在英吉利海峽的海圖上也畫了等深線，1737 年畫好、1752 年出版。

cards.en: From the riverbed to the mountain
cards.body_en: Mapmakers then used the same idea for land. In the 1770s the British mathematician Charles Hutton used lines of equal height while working on survey measurements of a Scottish mountain called Schiehallion. In 1791 a map of France by Jean-Louis Dupain-Triel showed the whole country with contour lines 20 meters apart. Today almost every topographic map uses them.
cards.body_zh: 後來製圖的人把同樣的想法用在陸地上。1770 年代，英國數學家哈頓在處理蘇格蘭一座叫希哈林的山的測量資料時，用了等高的線。1791 年，杜潘－特里耶爾的一張法國地圖，用每隔 20 公尺一條的等高線畫出整個國家。今天，幾乎每一張地形圖都用等高線。

cards.body_en: Taiwan's 1:25,000 topographic maps, made by the National Land Surveying and Mapping Center, draw an ordinary contour line every 10 meters and a thicker index contour every 50 meters. Where the land is very flat, they add extra lines every 5 meters. On maps with a smaller scale, the lines are spaced farther apart: 20 and 100 meters at 1:50,000.
cards.body_zh: 內政部國土測繪中心製作的 1/25,000 經建版地形圖，每 10 公尺畫一條首曲線、每 50 公尺畫一條加粗的計曲線；地勢很平的地方，再加每 5 公尺一條的間曲線。比例尺越小的地圖，線隔得越開：1/50,000 是 20 公尺和 100 公尺。

cards.en: How tall is Yushan, and tall from where?
cards.body_en: The sea around Taiwan is not exactly the same height everywhere, because of currents such as the Kuroshio. So Taiwan measures every height from one place: the average sea level at the Keelung tide station, worked out from tide records from 1957 to 1991. From that zero, careful leveling surveys found Yushan's main peak to be 3,951.798 m in 2003, 3,952.430 m in 2017, and 3,952.433 m in 2022. The numbers are for the survey mark at the summit; the top of the stone monument there is about 1 meter higher.
cards.body_zh: 台灣四周的海面並不是每個地方都一樣高，因為黑潮等因素會影響海面。所以台灣的高度都從同一個地方算起：基隆潮位站的平均海水面，用 1957 年到 1991 年的潮汐資料算出來。從這個零點出發，國土測繪中心用最精密的水準測量量出玉山主峰：2003 年 3,951.798 公尺、2017 年 3,952.430 公尺、2022 年 3,952.433 公尺。這些數字是山頂三角點的高度；主峰石碑的頂端大約再高 1 公尺。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (2018). The words contour line (等高線) and topographic map (地形圖) do not appear in the curriculum itself, and the elementary-school content has no entry about them. The links below are our reading of the closest entries.
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年發布）。課綱本身沒有出現「等高線」和「地形圖」這兩個詞，國小階段也沒有相關的條目；下面列的是最接近的條目，和本課的連結是本教材的解讀。

items.text: 臺灣主要地形的分布與特色。
items.note_en: Contour lines are one of the main ways maps show where Taiwan's mountains, hills, and plains are.
items.note_zh: 等高線是地圖呈現台灣的山地、丘陵、平原分布的主要方法之一。

items.area: 社會領域・地理（普通型高中必修）
items.text: 問題探究：地圖判讀與使用。
items.note_en: Reading which path is steeper and drawing a profile are basic skills of map reading.
items.note_zh: 判斷哪條路比較陡、畫出剖面，都是讀地圖的基本功。

items.area: 社會領域・地理（普通型高中必修）
items.note_en: Summits, saddles, and valleys can be recognized from the pattern of contour lines.
items.note_zh: 山頂、鞍部、山谷，都能從等高線的樣子認出來。

myths.myth_en: A thick contour line marks a cliff or a special place.
myths.myth_zh: 粗的等高線代表懸崖或特別的地方。
myths.fact_en: On many maps every fifth line is simply drawn thicker and labeled, so readers can count heights quickly. It means nothing special about the ground.
myths.fact_zh: 很多地圖只是每五條線畫粗一條、標上高度，方便讀的人快速數高度，和地面本身沒有特別的關係。

myths.myth_en: Contour lines are real lines you can see on the ground.
myths.myth_zh: 等高線是地面上看得到的真的線。
myths.fact_en: They are imaginary, like the equator. Mapmakers measure heights and draw the lines. Our model shows how a rising sea could trace them.
myths.fact_zh: 等高線和赤道一樣是想像的線，是製圖的人量了高度之後畫出來的。我們的模型示範的是：如果海面升高，水邊會怎麼把它們描出來。

myths.myth_en: Where there are more contour lines, the mountain is bigger.
myths.myth_zh: 等高線越多的地方，山就越大。
myths.fact_en: The number of lines between two places shows how much height changes. How close together they are shows how steep it is. A map with a smaller contour interval simply has more lines.
myths.fact_zh: 兩地之間有幾條線，表示高度差多少；線擠得多近，表示有多陡。等高距比較小的地圖，線本來就比較多。

myths.myth_en: Contour lines can cross whenever the land is complicated.
myths.myth_zh: 地形複雜的時候，等高線可以交叉。
myths.fact_en: Each contour line joins points of one height, so lines of different heights never cross. Where a slope is extremely steep, the lines can come so close that they seem to merge.
myths.fact_zh: 每一條等高線連的都是同一個高度的點，所以不同高度的線不會交叉。坡非常陡的地方，線會靠得很近，看起來像疊在一起。

tricks.body_en: Walk along a contour line and you never go up or down.
tricks.body_zh: 沿著一條等高線走，永遠不會上坡也不會下坡。

tricks.title_en: Close is steep, far is gentle
tricks.body_en: Crowded lines, hard climb. Spread-out lines, easy walk.
tricks.body_zh: 線擠在一起，爬得辛苦；線分得很開，走得輕鬆。

tricks.body_en: The smallest ring in the middle is the top.
tricks.body_zh: 最裡面那個最小的圈，就是山頂。

tricks.body_en: Where lines cross a stream they bend into a V, and the point of the V aims upstream.
tricks.body_zh: 等高線經過河谷時會彎成 V 字形，V 的尖端指向上游。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before the Activities · 做活動之前

safety.en: An adult cuts the potato or the clay with a knife. Students use plastic tools and keep their fingers away from any blade.
safety.zh: 切馬鈴薯或黏土由大人用刀切；學生用塑膠工具，手指遠離刀刃。

safety.en: Wipe up spilled water right away so that nobody slips, and keep water away from electrical outlets and devices.
safety.zh: 水灑出來馬上擦乾，免得有人滑倒；水要遠離插座和電器。

safety.en: Use a waterproof marker on the model and wash your hands afterward.
safety.zh: 在模型上畫線用防水筆，做完要洗手。

safety.en: If you walk a real slope to feel the difference, stay on marked paths and go with an adult.
safety.zh: 如果到真的坡地上走走、感受坡度的差別，要走在步道上，並且有大人陪同。

materials.en: A lump of modeling clay shaped into a mountain, or half a potato
materials.zh: 一團捏成山形的黏土，或半顆馬鈴薯

materials.en: A clear plastic box taller than the mountain
materials.zh: 一個比山高的透明塑膠盒

materials.en: A ruler, a waterproof marker, and a cup of water
materials.zh: 一把尺、一支防水筆、一杯水

materials.en: A sheet of clear plastic and a dry-erase marker
materials.zh: 一張透明片和一支白板筆

steps.en: Put the mountain in the box. Stand the ruler in a corner of the box.
steps.zh: 把山放進盒子裡，把尺立在盒子的一角。

steps.en: Pour in water until it is 1 cm deep. With the marker, trace the water's edge around the mountain.
steps.zh: 倒水到 1 公分深。用防水筆沿著山邊的水線畫一圈。

steps.en: Add water to 2 cm, then 3 cm, and so on, tracing a new line each time, until the top is under water.
steps.zh: 加水到 2 公分、3 公分……每次都畫一圈新的線，直到山頂淹沒。

steps.en: Pour the water out. Lay the clear sheet over the top of the box and look straight down. Copy the lines onto the sheet.
steps.zh: 把水倒掉。把透明片蓋在盒子上，從正上方往下看，把線描到透明片上。

steps.en: Label each line with its height in centimeters. Where are the lines closest together? Feel the mountain there.
steps.zh: 在每一條線旁邊標上高度（公分）。哪裡的線最擠？用手摸摸那裡的山坡。

activities.tip_en: This is the same idea as the 3D model: each line was once the edge of the water. A 1 cm interval on a 10 cm mountain gives about ten lines.
activities.tip_zh: 這和 3D 模型是同一個道理：每一條線都曾經是水邊。10 公分高的山、每 1 公分一條線，大約會有十條線。

materials.en: The contour map you drew on the clear sheet, or a printed one
materials.zh: 你畫在透明片上的等高線圖，或一張印好的圖

materials.en: A strip of paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 一張紙條和一枝鉛筆

materials.en: Graph paper
materials.zh: 方格紙

steps.en: Draw a straight line across the map, from one side of the mountain to the other.
steps.zh: 在地圖上畫一條直線，從山的一邊畫到另一邊。

steps.en: Lay the edge of the paper strip along the line. Make a tick wherever a contour line crosses it, and write the height beside each tick.
steps.zh: 把紙條的邊貼著這條線，每遇到一條等高線就畫一個記號，旁邊寫上高度。

steps.en: Move the strip to the graph paper. Above each tick, put a dot at the right height.
steps.zh: 把紙條移到方格紙上，在每個記號的正上方、對應的高度點一個點。

steps.en: Join the dots with a smooth curve. You have drawn the profile.
steps.zh: 用平滑的曲線把點連起來，你就畫出了剖面。

steps.en: Check your profile with the “From Contour Lines to a Side View” map on this page.
steps.zh: 用本頁的「從等高線到剖面」地圖，檢查你畫的剖面。

activities.tip_en: Where the ticks on the strip are close together, the profile climbs steeply. This is the same rule as reading the map.
activities.tip_zh: 紙條上記號擠在一起的地方，剖面就爬得很陡。和讀地圖是同一個規則。

lessons.title: How Do You Read a Map?
lessons.blurb_en: Turn a 3D model of an island town until you look straight down and the buildings turn into symbols. Then measure distances with the scale and find your way with the north arrow and the legend.
lessons.blurb_zh: 把一座小島小鎮的 3D 模型轉到正上方，看房子變成地圖符號。再用比例尺量距離，用北方箭頭和圖例找路。
lessons.big_idea_en: Every map is a view from above, made smaller and drawn with symbols. To read any map, first find three things: the scale, which way is north, and the legend.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 每一張地圖都是從上往下看、縮小、再用符號畫出來的。看任何一張地圖，先找三件事：比例尺、哪邊是北、圖例。

lab.title_en: From a Model to a Map
lab.how_en: Press “Look straight down,” or pull the slider, and watch the camera turn until it looks straight down on the town. The buildings, trees, and lighthouse fade away and map symbols take their place. Choose a smaller area to see the same place at a larger scale, drag left or right to turn the island and watch the north arrow, and click a symbol in the legend to find it. The island and town are imaginary.
lab.how_zh: 按「轉到正上方」或拉動滑桿，看鏡頭慢慢轉到小鎮的正上方。房子、樹和燈塔淡出，換成地圖符號。選小一點的範圍，就是用大一點的比例尺看同一個地方；左右拖曳轉動小島，看北方箭頭怎麼跟著轉；點圖例裡的符號，找找它在哪裡。這座島和小鎮都是虛構的。

legend.en: North arrow: which way is north
Scale bar: how long a distance on the map is on the ground
legend.zh: 圖形比例尺：地圖上的長度在地面上是多遠

legend.en: Map symbols, explained in the legend
legend.zh: 地圖符號，意思寫在圖例裡

lab.scale_en: The island is 10 km across. Heights in the model are drawn 1.5 times taller than they really are. The ratio scales assume the view is printed 20 cm wide.
lab.scale_zh: 這座島寬 10 公里，模型裡的高度畫成實際的 1.5 倍。比例尺的數字，是假設這個畫面印成 20 公分寬。
lab.credit_html: The island, the town, and every name on this page are imaginary. The map symbols were drawn for this page and are not any agency's official symbols. · 這座島、小鎮和頁面上所有的地名都是虛構的。地圖符號是本頁自己畫的，不是任何機關的官方圖例。

paras: Imagine you are standing on a hill above a small town. You can see roofs, roads, a river, and fields. Now imagine rising higher and higher until you are looking straight down. The town looks flat, and everything in it looks small. A map is a drawing of that view from above, made smaller so that it fits on a sheet of paper or a screen.

A map cannot show things as they really look, so it uses symbols. A blue line can mean a river, a small flag can mean a school, and green with little dots can mean a forest. Different maps use different symbols, so every good map has a legend, also called a key. The legend is a small table that tells you what each symbol means. When you meet a map you have never seen, the legend is the first place to look.

The second thing to find is direction. On most maps, north is at the top, south is at the bottom, east is on the right, and west is on the left. Between them are northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest. But not every map is drawn that way, so look for a north arrow. If the arrow points somewhere else, turn the map in your mind until the arrow points up.

The third thing is the scale. The scale tells you how much smaller the map is than the real ground. A scale of 1:25,000 means that 1 centimeter on the map stands for 25,000 centimeters on the ground, which is 250 meters. Many maps also have a scale bar, a short line marked with a distance such as 500 meters. If the map is enlarged or shrunk, the bar changes with it and stays correct, but the number 1:25,000 does not. You can lay a ruler or the edge of a piece of paper along the bar to measure any distance on the map.

The same place can be drawn at different scales. A map of a whole country fits on one page only if it is made much smaller, so it shows less detail. A map of one neighborhood can show every building. Mapmakers call the second kind a large-scale map, because the fraction 1/5,000 is larger than 1/500,000. This sounds backward to many people, so it is worth remembering.

With these three things, you can answer real questions. How far is it from the school to the harbor? Use the scale. Which way should you walk from the bridge to reach the lighthouse? Use the north arrow. Is the green patch beside the road a forest or a rice field? Use the legend. Reading a map is not memorizing it. It is asking the map good questions.
paras_zh: 想像你站在一座小鎮旁邊的山丘上，看得到屋頂、道路、一條河和田地。現在想像你越升越高，直到從正上方往下看。小鎮看起來是平的，每樣東西都變得很小。地圖就是把這個從上往下看的樣子畫下來，再縮小到一張紙或一個螢幕放得下。
地圖沒辦法把東西照它真正的樣子畫出來，所以用符號。藍色的線可以代表河，小旗子可以代表學校，綠色加上小點點可以代表森林。不同的地圖用不同的符號，所以好的地圖都有圖例。圖例是一張小表，告訴你每個符號代表什麼。遇到一張沒看過的地圖，第一個要看的就是圖例。
第二件要找的是方位。大多數的地圖上方是北、下方是南、右邊是東、左邊是西；它們之間還有東北、東南、西南、西北。但不是每一張地圖都這樣畫，所以要找北方箭頭（學術名詞叫「指北標」）。如果箭頭指向別的方向，就在心裡把地圖轉一轉，讓箭頭朝上。
第三件是比例尺。比例尺告訴你地圖比真正的地面縮小了多少。比例尺 1:25,000 的意思是：地圖上的 1 公分，代表地面上的 25,000 公分，也就是 250 公尺。很多地圖還有圖形比例尺，是一小段標著距離（例如 500 公尺）的線。地圖被放大或縮小時，這段線會跟著一起變，所以仍然是對的；1:25,000 這個數字就不對了。把尺或一張紙的邊對著它，就能量地圖上任何一段距離。
同一個地方可以用不同的比例尺來畫。整個國家的地圖要縮得很小才放得進一頁，所以畫得比較粗略；一個街區的地圖可以把每一棟房子都畫出來。製圖的人把後面那一種叫做「大比例尺」地圖，因為 1/5,000 這個分數比 1/500,000 大。很多人覺得這說法剛好反過來，所以值得記住。
有了這三件事，就能回答真正的問題。從學校到港口有多遠？用比例尺。從橋要往哪個方向走才會到燈塔？用北方箭頭。公路旁邊那一片綠色是森林還是稻田？用圖例。讀地圖不是把地圖背起來，而是向地圖問好問題。
questions: Why does every good map need a legend?
A map has the scale 1:50,000. Two towns are 6 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they on the ground?
Which shows more detail: a map at 1:5,000 or a map at 1:500,000? Which one is called the large-scale map?
answers: Different maps use different symbols, so the legend tells you what each symbol means on this particular map.
The 1:5,000 map shows more detail, because it covers a smaller area. It is the large-scale map, because 1/5,000 is a larger fraction than 1/500,000.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.en: A map is a view from above
parts.text_en: Watch the camera turn until it looks straight down. The buildings and trees fade, and symbols take their place.
parts.text_zh: 看鏡頭慢慢轉到正上方。房子和樹淡出，換成符號。

parts.text_en: The school is highlighted on the map and in the legend. Click other symbols in the legend to find them too.
parts.text_zh: 學校在地圖上和圖例裡都亮了起來。點圖例裡的其他符號，也找找看。

parts.text_en: Zoom to the neighborhood. The view is 1 km wide instead of 10 km, so a 20 cm print would be 1:5,000. Watch the scale bar change.
parts.text_zh: 拉近到街區。畫面寬 1 公里而不是 10 公里，印成 20 公分寬就是 1:5,000。注意圖形比例尺怎麼改變。
